todaysEvents.delta: Al Jazeera's Sep 6 report records three Iranian tankers struck by CENTCOM, missiles fired at a US carrier and destroyer, and attacks on three tankers plus three US-linked vessels; no signed commercial reopening or verified route clearance is approved.

todaysEvents.summary: Brent and WTI soften in live quotes
todaysEvents.delta: Yahoo Finance shows Brent at $108.14 (-0.56%) and WTI at $104.80 (-0.97%) on Sep 16. Both remain elevated versus pre-shock levels while route-disruption risk remains unresolved.

todaysEvents.summary: Qatar force majeure runs into November
todaysEvents.delta: LNG Industry reported on Sep 1 that five additional QatarEnergy cargoes were affected, bringing the total to 29 and extending the period into early November; 21 were replaced as of Aug 28.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and Oman's traffic-management framework, reported at a 'final stage' with IMO registration expected within days, is signed and monitored; a restored, verified reopening lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained into early November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The Oman framework registers but traffic stays selective under Iranian fees, sanctions pressure and the threatened exclusion zone; Brent holds $85-105 and JKM stays elevated while Qatar's force majeure runs into early November.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Iran declares and enforces its threatened Hormuz exclusion zone, the Oman framework collapses, or the tanker war widens into a broader multi-front exchange; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
